title: Trace a RocketMQ delivery from route lookup to recovery
description: Select an operating condition to see which path is active, what RocketMQ can know, and where the application must preserve business correctness.

nodes.label: Producer
nodes.detail: Creates a typed message with a topic, stable business event ID, and a message group when per-entity FIFO is required. A send timeout is an unknown outcome until reconciled.

nodes.label: RocketMQ Proxy
nodes.detail: Provides the current gRPC client endpoint. It can run with a Broker or as a stateless cluster, depending on the deployment mode.

nodes.label: NameServer cluster
nodes.detail: Receives Broker registrations and supplies topic routing metadata. Run multiple instances so one failed NameServer does not remove route discovery.

nodes.label: Broker topic
nodes.detail: Persists messages in MessageQueues, serves matching consumers, tracks retry state, and keeps messages according to node storage duration rather than consumption status.

nodes.label: Consumer group
nodes.detail: Runs one logical subscriber with shared behavior. A success result advances processing; a failure or timeout can make the message available for another delivery.

nodes.label: Order store
nodes.detail: Applies the domain mutation. A unique event receipt committed with the mutation turns repeated delivery into one visible business result.

nodes.label: Retry state
nodes.detail: Represents a failed or timed-out delivery waiting to become ready again. Retry timing and state transitions depend on the consumer type.

nodes.label: Dead-letter queue
nodes.detail: Receives a message after the configured retry limit. It isolates repeatedly failing work but requires diagnosis, repair, and a controlled replay procedure.

scenarios.label: Healthy delivery
scenarios.summary: The producer reaches the 5.x Proxy, routing metadata identifies the Broker, and the consumer commits one business effect before reporting success.
scenarios.result: The message path completes, but correctness still depends on the consumer reporting success only after its business work is durable. Monitor the final effect, not only the broker acknowledgement.

scenarios.label: Route lookup unavailable
scenarios.summary: The NameServer cluster cannot answer a new route lookup. Existing cached routes may be temporary, but clients cannot rely on learning a new or changed Broker route.
scenarios.result: Run multiple NameServers and alert on registration and route-refresh failures. Treat cached routing as a bounded continuity aid, not a replacement for a healthy routing control plane.

scenarios.label: Timeout after commit
scenarios.summary: The consumer commits the order update, but its success result is lost or late. RocketMQ cannot observe the external commit and makes the message available again.
scenarios.result: Redelivery is the correct broker behavior for an unknown outcome. A stable event ID and an atomic receipt in the order store prevent the replay from applying a second charge or state transition.

scenarios.label: Poison message
scenarios.summary: A permanent schema or business-rule error fails every attempt. After the configured retry limit, the broker isolates the message in the consumer group's DLQ.
scenarios.result: Quarantine lets healthy traffic continue. Diagnose the payload and handler version, repair the cause, preserve the event ID, and replay at a bounded rate with reconciliation.
